record.cohortNote: Reference life table for the birth country and sex; a population model, not a prediction for this individual or a historical birth cohort.
record.annualNote: Snapshots at each age. Income, costs and budget surplus describe the annual household budget at that point; they exclude one-off purchases, investment returns and medical bills. Older saves may have no detailed snapshots.
grain.title: The pattern of this life
grain.mixed: Two or more pairs are near the center (40–60), so this life has a mixed pattern.
grain.short: Fewer than three recorded adult years: there is not enough evidence to assign one of the sixteen life patterns.
grain.note: A reading of this simulated life, not a personality test or a ranking. These four pairs use recorded years and choices; they are a transparent heuristic, not calibrated against other players.
companion.note: Four fictional people born at the same time. Where their observed story was still unfinished, an independent deterministic simulation completes it. These continuations do not change your life or predict real futures.
grain.evidence0: {together} completed adult years focused on relationships; {work} on career. Other focuses are neutral on this pair.
grain.evidence1: {away} of {years} recorded adult years lived outside the birth country.
grain.evidence2: {exposed} years with stocks or business allocation; {transitions} adjacent years with a job or country change, or a health or happiness change of at least 10 points.
grain.evidence3: {saving} years saving more than 10% of annual income; {study} years focused on knowledge. Counts may overlap; the score is capped.
grain.formula: Together–Work compares years focused on relationships and career. Roots–Wind uses the share of adult years abroad. Stillness–Waves combines risk allocation years (up to 50 points) and recorded transitions (250 × transitions ÷ years, capped at 100). Today–Tomorrow counts years with a budget surplus above 10% of income plus knowledge-focused years, capped at 100.

decision.healthClinic: {name} is unwell. Choose a care plan and allow time to recover.
decision.healthFollowup: {name} is due for a review of a long-term condition. Keeping up with care can reduce its impact over the coming years.
decision.healthHospital: {name} needs hospital care. Specialist treatment offers more support but may leave a larger bill.
decision.healthIcu: {name} is critically ill. The ICU team explains the available care. Treatment may improve the chance of recovery, but the outcome is uncertain.
decision.healthNeonatal: {name} was born early and needs help breathing, feeding, and staying warm. The family must choose the available neonatal care.
event.healthNeonatal: {name} arrives earlier than expected. A neonatal care team helps the family understand what comes next.
event.healthIcu: {name} becomes critically ill and needs care in an intensive care unit (ICU).
event.healthAdmission: {name} needs medical attention. The family considers treatment and its cost.
event.healthFollowup: A planned review gives {name} a chance to adjust care for a long-term condition.
event.healthTreatment: A care plan is chosen for {name}. The household pays or borrows {amount} for treatment.
event.healthDischarge: {name} is stable enough to leave acute care. Recovery will take time.
event.healthRecovered: {name} completes the recovery period and returns to everyday life.
event.healthChronic: Recovery brings a lasting change: a long-term condition now needs regular attention.
event.healthManaged: The review helps keep the condition under control. The next review is scheduled.
event.healthMissed: Care is postponed. The condition becomes harder to manage, and another review will be needed sooner.
event.healthLoss: {name} reaches the end of life during this illness. The family remembers their time together.

epilogue.nursery.title: A room full of light
epilogue.nursery.0: Morning light reaches the room where {name} rests.
epilogue.nursery.1: Someone moves a curtain so the light is softer.
epilogue.nursery.2: The smallest moments can hold a great deal of love.
epilogue.school.title: One ordinary afternoon
epilogue.school.0: {name} finds a small patch of sunshine by the window.
epilogue.school.1: Outside, the afternoon carries on at its own pace.
epilogue.school.2: For this imagined moment, there is nothing more to do.
epilogue.city.title: The long way home
epilogue.city.1: A shopkeeper is pulling down a sunshade. Somewhere, a bicycle bell rings.
epilogue.city.2: There is still enough daylight to take the long way home.
epilogue.beach.title: A place by the water
epilogue.beach.0: {name} watches a line of foam disappear into the sand.
epilogue.beach.1: A small shell turns over in the next wave.
epilogue.beach.2: The afternoon asks for nothing in return.
epilogue.home.title: The window left open
epilogue.home.0: {name} leaves the window open a little longer.
epilogue.home.1: A cup is cooling on the table. Light moves across the wall.
epilogue.home.2: An ordinary room, holding an ordinary day.
epilogue.farm.title: Something growing
epilogue.farm.0: {name} notices a new leaf beside the path.
epilogue.farm.1: It was not there yesterday, or perhaps nobody noticed.
epilogue.park.title: A quiet page
epilogue.park.0: {name} settles beside a tree with a book.
epilogue.park.1: A breeze turns the corner of a page before it can be read.
epilogue.park.2: There is time to find the sentence again.
epilogue.music.title: An unfinished tune
epilogue.music.0: {name} taps out a tune on the edge of the table.
epilogue.music.1: The melody stops, then finds its way back.
epilogue.music.2: A little music stays in the room after the hands are still.
